summary: Iter16 retest CONFIRMS asyncio.to_thread fix produces TRUE parallel uploads. 5/6 pytest passed (1 skipped — no error timestamps to compare because all sample uploads SUCCEEDED, which itself is superior evidence). Timing evidence: N=1=2.39s, N=5=4.46s (would be ~12s serial → 2.7x speedup), N=12=7.77s (would be ~29s serial → 3.7x speedup — matches ~3 waves of Semaphore(5)). Additional proof: urllib3 emits 8 'Connection pool is full, discarding connection: api.cloudinary.com' warnings clustered within ~500ms during the N=5 and N=12 runs — this only happens when multiple threads make simultaneous HTTP requests, proving the sync SDK is running in parallel worker threads. Iter15 sequential ~230ms-apart pattern is GONE. All regressions pass: SYNC_PATH_TIMEOUT_SEC=25.0 verified, hashtag 'travel' search/start=25.98s (<30s), export CSV 200 OK, single-reel upload 2.39s (no regression from to_thread overhead).

minor.issue: urllib3 'Connection pool is full, discarding connection: api.cloudinary.com. Connection pool size: 1' warnings during parallel uploads. Functionally harmless (urllib3 falls back to new connection) but noisy in logs and mildly inefficient. Optionally configure cloudinary.config(api_proxy=..., ...) or pass a urllib3 PoolManager with pool_maxsize>=5 to match Semaphore(5).

action_items: None blocking. Optionally: bump urllib3 pool_maxsize for cloudinary client to 5+ to eliminate 'Connection pool is full' warnings during parallel uploads.
